mentions.heading: If we do not deliver new products, services, technologies, and customer experiences in response to increased competition, our business could suffer
mentions.risk_name: Technology disruption from new automotive competitors
mentions.detail: Start-ups, tech-backed software and ridesharing entrants; need to commercialize EVs, AV, connected services and AI beyond core ICE business
mentions.quote: To successfully execute our long-term strategy, we must continue to develop and commercialize new products and services, including products and services that are outside of our historically core ICE business, such as EVs and AV capabilities, software-enabled connected services, future features and services based on AI, and other new businesses.

mentions.heading: Our ability to attract and retain talented and highly skilled employees is critical to our success
mentions.risk_name: Shortage of skilled software engineering talent
mentions.detail: Vehicles and connected services rely on complex software and hardware; competitive market for skilled workers
mentions.quote: In particular, our vehicles and connected services increasingly rely on software and hardware that is highly technical and complex, and our success in this area is dependent upon our ability to retain and recruit the best talent.

mentions.heading: Our ability to maintain profitability is dependent upon timely funding and introduction of new vehicle models
mentions.risk_name: New vehicle launch and acceptance risk
mentions.detail: Development cycle of two years or more; EV launches; high fixed costs from PP&E investment
mentions.quote: The new vehicle development process can take two years or more, and a number of factors may lengthen that time period.

mentions.heading: Our long-term EV strategy is dependent upon our ability to profitably deliver a strategic portfolio of EVs
mentions.risk_name: EV strategy execution and battery costs
mentions.detail: Must cut battery cell and pack costs, source battery materials; losses recorded on EV-related inventory including battery cells
mentions.quote: Our progress towards these objectives has impacted, and may continue to impact, the need to record losses on our EV-related inventory, including battery cells.

mentions.heading: The success of our long-term EV strategy is dependent on consumer adoption of EVs
mentions.risk_name: Slow EV adoption after incentive termination
mentions.detail: US EV tax incentive termination slowed adoption; capacity realignment charges of $1.6B and $6.0B in Q3/Q4 2025; $7.9B total GMNA charges
mentions.quote: For the year ended December 31, 2025, we recorded total charges in GMNA of $7.9 billion.

drivers.name: consumer tax incentives for EV purchases

mentions.heading: Our near-term profitability is dependent upon the success of our current line of vehicles, particularly full-size ICE SUVs and pickups
mentions.risk_name: Profit concentration in full-size ICE trucks
mentions.detail: Highest margins from full-size ICE SUVs and pickups, which fund EV/AV growth; vulnerable to oil price spikes and fuel economy rules
mentions.quote: Any near-term shift in consumer preferences toward smaller, more fuel-efficient vehicles, whether as a result of increases in the price of oil or any sustained shortage of oil, including as a result of global political instability (such as related to ongoing conflicts globally), concerns about fuel consumption or GHG emissions, or other reasons, could weaken the demand for our higher margin vehicles.

mentions.heading: We operate in a highly competitive industry that has historically had excess manufacturing capacity
mentions.detail: High fixed labor costs and collective bargaining limits on closing plants force subsidized financing, incentives, price cuts
mentions.quote: In light of any excess capacity and high fixed costs, many industry participants have attempted to sell more vehicles by providing subsidized financing or leasing programs, offering marketing incentives, or reducing vehicle prices.

mentions.heading: Need for North American-focused supply chain for ICE and EVs
mentions.risk_name: North American raw materials supply shortfall
mentions.detail: Raw material demand exceeds North American capacity; multi-year supply agreements and supplier investments require high inventory and long-term purchase commitments
mentions.quote: These agreements may require us to hold higher-than-normal levels of raw materials inventory and to make long-term commitments to purchase raw materials. Expected demand for these raw materials currently exceeds the North American capacity of the existing supply chain.

mentions.heading: Low-cost manufacturers from China and India entering markets
mentions.detail: Chinese and Indian manufacturers compete in emerging and established markets, already hurting pricing and share
mentions.quote: Manufacturers in countries that have lower production costs, such as China and India, have become competitors in key emerging markets and have begun offering their products in established markets, as well as low-cost alternatives to established entry-level automobiles.

mentions.heading: Foreign government policies and import tariffs
mentions.detail: Foreign governments may favor domestic manufacturers over GM and JV partners; tariffs may challenge global business
mentions.quote: In addition, foreign governments may decide to implement tax and other policies that favor their domestic manufacturers at the expense of international manufacturers, including GM and its joint venture partners. Introduction or modification of import tariffs or tariff-related measures may lead to further challenges for GM and our global business.

mentions.heading: Refocused AV strategy on personal vehicles dependent on mitigating technological, operational, regulatory and competitive risks
mentions.risk_name: Autonomous vehicle development and commercialization risk
mentions.detail: Wound down Cruise robotaxi after Dec 2024 refocus; acquired Cruise minority stake Feb 2025; AV/ADAS still capital intensive, needs AI talent and data
mentions.quote: While we expect our refocused AV strategy to be less capital intensive than the Cruise robotaxi plan, we expect that our AV and ADAS development activities will continue to require significant capital investments and remain subject to a variety of risks inherent with the development of new technologies, including our ability to continue to develop self-driving software and hardware; attract and retain key software talent with expertise in AI and machine learning; access sufficient capital; access high-quality data to train the AI models deployed in our AV and ADAS technologies; and respond to significant competition from both established automotive companies and technology companies, some of which may have more resources and capital to devote to AV technologies than we do.

mentions.heading: Risks associated with climate change, GHG regulation and changing consumer demand
mentions.risk_name: Evolving emissions regulation and EV demand shift
mentions.detail: Federal easing of emissions/fuel economy rules slowed North American EV demand; possible emissions credit purchases or penalties; ICE cost/demand pressure
mentions.quote: In addition, the reduction in the stringency of emissions regulations has slowed and may continue to slow consumer demand for EVs in North America. These requirements may increase the cost of, and/or diminish demand for, our ICE vehicles.

mentions.heading: Climate change-driven severe weather may disrupt production and demand
mentions.risk_name: Severe weather disruption from climate change
mentions.detail: Storms, droughts, wildfires could disrupt GM plants, supplier production and logistics, dealer operations and customer demand
mentions.quote: In addition, increased intensity, frequency, or duration of storms, droughts, wildfires, or other severe weather events as a result of climate change may disrupt our production and the production, logistics, cost, and procurement of products from our suppliers, timely delivery of vehicles to customers and operations of our dealers, and could negatively impact working conditions at our plants and those of our suppliers and dealers.

mentions.heading: Our business is highly dependent upon global automobile market sales volume, which can be volatile
mentions.risk_name: Auto sales volume volatility with fixed costs
mentions.detail: High fixed structural costs magnify small sales declines; drivers include used vehicle prices, financing, rates, fuel costs
mentions.quote: Because we have a high proportion of relatively fixed structural costs, small changes in sales volume can have a disproportionately large effect on our profitability.

mentions.heading: Inflationary pressures and high prices and uncertain availability of commodities and inputs
mentions.risk_name: Commodity and semiconductor input cost inflation
mentions.detail: Steel, precious and non-ferrous metals, semiconductors raise production costs; may not pass on to customers
mentions.quote: Increases in prices, including as a result of inflation and rising interest rates, for commodities, raw materials, energy, or other inputs that we and our suppliers use in manufacturing products, systems, components, and parts, such as steel, precious metals, non-ferrous metals, critical minerals, or other similar raw materials, or electrical subcomponents, including transistors, diodes, and other semiconductors, or increases in logistics and related costs, have led and may continue to lead to higher production costs for parts, components, and vehicles.

mentions.heading: Cost and availability of critical EV battery materials
mentions.risk_name: EV battery critical mineral supply constraints
mentions.detail: Lithium, nickel, cobalt, rare earth metal cost or shortage could raise EV costs and impede EV strategy
mentions.quote: In addition, elevated cost, or reduced availability, of critical materials for our EV propulsion systems, including lithium, nickel, cobalt, and certain rare earth metals, may lead to higher production costs for our EVs and could impede our ability to successfully deliver on our EV strategy.

mentions.heading: Tariffs applicable to the automotive industry continue to evolve
mentions.detail: US tariffs on vehicles, parts, materials; USMCA review; mitigation via production changes won't fully offset; possible restructuring and impairments
mentions.quote: New or existing trade agreements, including the ongoing review of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, may also impact the tariff rate applicable to goods imported by GM or our suppliers. Additionally, certain tariffs are subject to pending legal challenges.

mentions.heading: Our business in China subjects us to unique operational, competitive, regulatory, and economic risks.
mentions.risk_name: China JV competition and restructuring losses
mentions.detail: China JV impairment $2.1B and equity losses $2.0B in 2024, $0.6B charges 2025; SGM expects more restructuring in 2026
mentions.quote: As a result of certain restructuring actions previously announced in December 2024, we recorded an other-than-temporary impairment of our equity interests of $2.1 billion and additional equity losses of $2.0 billion in the year ended December 31, 2024, and we recorded charges of $0.6 billion in the year ended December 31, 2025.

mentions.heading: Chinese government regulation and critical materials access
mentions.risk_name: Chinese regulation restricting critical materials access
mentions.detail: Chinese government may restrict non-Chinese access to critical materials; U.S.-China trade tensions; China integrated in global supply chain
mentions.quote: The Chinese government may adopt new regulations that may impact entities operating in China or the ability of non-Chinese entities to obtain critical materials from China, potentially with little advance notice.

mentions.heading: We benefit from many ongoing joint ventures and other strategic business relationships over which we may have limited control.
mentions.risk_name: EV raw material offtake obligation exposure
mentions.detail: Offtake agreements obligate purchases of EV raw materials; lower EV volumes or battery tech changes could hurt cash flows; supplier investments may lose value
mentions.quote: If we are unable to utilize or otherwise monetize the raw materials we are obligated to purchase under these offtake agreements, whether as a result of lower than expected EV production volumes, lower than expected rates of consumer adoption, changes in battery technology that reduce the need for certain raw materials, or other reasons, it could materially adversely affect our cash flows and increase our inventory.

mentions.heading: Operations carried out by joint ventures in China, Korea and battery sourcing
mentions.risk_name: Joint venture partner and control risk
mentions.detail: Major operations in China and Korea via JVs; China JV agreement expires 2027, renegotiation ongoing; battery and raw material JVs in U.S./Canada
mentions.quote: Our primary joint venture agreement for our China JVs expires in 2027, and we are in negotiations with our partner for a new agreement.

mentions.heading: Limited control over joint venture actions and compliance
mentions.risk_name: Joint venture compliance and misconduct exposure
mentions.detail: Minority interests limit control; JVs may not follow GM governance, reporting or compliance; potential fines and reputational harm
mentions.quote: As a result, we may be unable to prevent violations of applicable laws or other misconduct by a joint venture, adverse human rights or other impacts, or the failure to satisfy contractual obligations by one or more parties.

mentions.heading: The international scale and footprint of our operations expose us to additional risks
mentions.detail: Tensions between China and U.S. may restrict dividend repatriation and technology exports
mentions.quote: (5) political and economic tensions between governments and changes in international economic policies, including restrictions on the repatriation of dividends or in the export of technology, especially between China and the U.S.;

mentions.heading: Tariffs and trade barriers on global operations
mentions.risk_name: Import tariffs and trade barrier costs
mentions.detail: New or higher tariffs on products imported into or exported from the U.S.; free trade agreement changes; integrated global supply chain
mentions.quote: (6) changes to customs requirements or procedures (e.g., inspections) or new or higher tariffs, for example, on products imported into or exported from the U.S., including under U.S. or other trade laws or measures, or other key markets;

mentions.heading: Differing local product and certification requirements
mentions.risk_name: Divergent vehicle emissions and EV regulations
mentions.detail: Government certification on fuel economy, emissions, EVs, AVs, connected services and safety varies by country
mentions.quote: (10) differing local product preferences and product requirements, including government certification requirements related to, among other things, fuel economy, vehicle emissions, EVs and AVs, connected services, and safety;

mentions.heading: Export controls, sanctions and anti-corruption laws
mentions.detail: Exposure to U.S. and foreign export controls, sanctions, foreign investment rules and FCPA
mentions.quote: (12) impacts on our operations or liabilities resulting from U.S. and foreign laws and regulations, including, but not limited to, those related to the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and certain other anti-corruption laws;

mentions.heading: Currency, macroeconomic and catastrophic event risks abroad
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: (8) changes in foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates; (9) economic downturns or significant changes in macroeconomic conditions in the countries in which we operate;

mentions.heading: Any significant disruption at one of our manufacturing facilities could disrupt our production schedule.
mentions.detail: Facilities model/market-specific; no plant builds full range; certain facilities disproportionately drive profitability; hard to shift production
mentions.quote: We may not be able to easily shift production to other facilities or to make up for lost production.

mentions.heading: Unionized hourly workforce under collective bargaining agreements
mentions.detail: Substantially all hourly employees unionized; agreements negotiated including at local facility level
mentions.quote: In addition, substantially all of our hourly employees are represented by unions and covered by collective bargaining agreements that must be negotiated from time-to-time, including at the local facility level.

mentions.heading: Disruption in our suppliers' operations have disrupted, and could in the future disrupt, our production schedule.
mentions.detail: Just-in-time minimal inventory except battery raw material offtakes; single-source parts; higher margin vehicles at risk
mentions.quote: Other than with respect to certain of our offtake agreements with battery raw material suppliers, our use of “just-in-time” manufacturing processes typically allows us to maintain minimal inventory.

mentions.heading: Pandemics, epidemics, disease outbreaks, and other public health crises have disrupted our business and operations
mentions.detail: COVID-19 previously disrupted operations; risks include loan/lease defaults, lower auction pricing, impaired credit access
mentions.quote: In particular, we could experience, among other things: (1) continued or additional global supply disruptions; (2) labor disruptions or shortages; (3) an inability to manufacture; (4) an inability to sell to our customers; (5) a decline in showroom traffic and customer demand; (6) customer defaults on automobile loans and leases; (7) lower than expected pricing on vehicles sold at auction; and (8) an impaired ability to access credit and the capital markets.

mentions.heading: Competitors may independently develop products and services similar to ours
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Competitors may independently develop products and services similar to ours, and there are no guarantees that GM’s intellectual property rights would prevent competitors from independently developing or selling those products and services.

mentions.heading: Protection of intellectual property and patent enforcement claims
mentions.risk_name: Trade secret theft and patent infringement claims
mentions.detail: Unauthorized access attempts targeting trade secrets, heightened by AI; patent claims from non-practicing entities could bring damages or injunctions
mentions.quote: We sometimes face attempts to gain unauthorized access to our information technology networks and systems for the purpose of improperly acquiring our trade secrets or confidential business information, and may face increased such risk from the rapid evolution and adoption of AI.

mentions.heading: Security breaches, cyberattacks, and disruptions to IT systems and connected vehicles
mentions.risk_name: Cyberattacks on connected vehicles and IT systems
mentions.detail: Covers connected vehicles, GM Financial data, third-party providers; cannot patch all vulnerabilities; acquired companies may bring weak security
mentions.quote: We are unable to comprehensively apply patches or mitigate all such vulnerabilities before they may be exploited by a threat actor. We have also acquired and in the future may acquire companies with vulnerabilities or unsophisticated security measures, which exposes us to potentially significant cybersecurity risks.

mentions.heading: IT systems and connected products vulnerable to cyberattacks
mentions.risk_name: Cyberattacks on IT systems and connected products
mentions.detail: Regular phishing attacks experienced; AI-driven threat evolution; no material incident to date
mentions.quote: We and our third-party providers regularly experience cyberattacks and security incidents, such as phishing attacks, and we expect cyberattacks and incidents to continue in varying degrees, including due to the rapid evolution and adoption of AI.

mentions.heading: Security breaches and other disruptions of our in-vehicle systems could impact the safety of our customers
mentions.detail: Vehicle IT controls engine, steering, braking, batteries; hackers have attempted access; right-to-repair laws may expose vehicle systems
mentions.quote: Laws that would permit third-party access to vehicle data and related systems, including "right to repair" laws, could expose our vehicles and vehicle systems to third-party access without appropriate security measures in place, leading to new safety and security risks for our customers and reducing customer trust and confidence in our products.

mentions.heading: Enterprise data practices subject to complex, restrictive, punitive regulations
mentions.risk_name: Data privacy and AI regulation compliance
mentions.detail: Named CCPA/CPRA, EU GDPR, EU AI Act, UK Data Protection Act; compliance has significantly increased operating costs
mentions.quote: Complying with these new laws has significantly increased, and may continue to increase, our operating costs and is driving increased complexity in our operations.

mentions.heading: Extensive laws including vehicle emissions and fuel economy standards increase costs
mentions.risk_name: Emissions and fuel economy regulation costs
mentions.detail: Could limit profitable ICE sales, require credit purchases; risk of emissions credit impairment like prior CAFE credit impairment
mentions.quote: In addition, proposed regulatory changes to the GHG emissions standards could result in an impairment of our emissions credits, similar to the previous impairment we recognized related to our CAFE credits.

mentions.heading: Limits on ability to achieve fuel economy improvements
mentions.risk_name: EV technology adoption and battery supply limits
mentions.detail: EV infrastructure, consumer acceptance and battery raw material supply constrain profitable compliance
mentions.quote: There is no assurance that we will be able to produce and sell vehicles that use such new technologies on a profitable basis or that our customers will purchase such vehicles in the quantities necessary for us to comply with current or future regulatory requirements.

mentions.heading: Compliance costs and alleged violations of fuel economy or emission standards
mentions.risk_name: Fuel economy and emissions non-compliance penalties
mentions.detail: Alleged violations could bring recalls, fines, restricted offerings, facility idling; compliance costs not reasonably estimable
mentions.quote: Alleged violations of fuel economy or vehicle emission standards could result in legal proceedings, the recall of one or more of our products, negotiated remedial actions, fines and penalties, restricted product offerings, or a combination of any of those items.

drivers.name: fuel economy or vehicle emission standards

mentions.heading: Evolving regulation of advanced technologies including AVs
mentions.detail: AVs present novel issues for regulators; rules could impede commercialization and raise costs
mentions.quote: In addition, many of our advanced technologies, including AVs, present novel issues with which domestic and foreign regulators have only limited experience and will be subject to evolving regulatory frameworks.

mentions.heading: We could be materially adversely affected by unusual or significant litigation, governmental investigations, or other proceedings
mentions.detail: Product liability, warranty, class action defect, emissions, privacy, stockholder suits; see Note 16
mentions.quote: We are subject to legal proceedings in the U.S. and elsewhere involving various issues, including product liability lawsuits, warranty litigations, class action litigations alleging product defects, emissions litigations, privacy matters, stockholder litigations, labor and employment litigations, and claims and actions arising from restructurings and divestitures of operations and assets.

mentions.heading: Product safety recalls and alleged defects could materially adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: Recall costs amplified on global platforms; AV safety concerns could trigger investigations and reputational damage
mentions.quote: The costs to complete a recall could be exacerbated to the extent that such action relates to a global platform.

mentions.heading: Supplier part quality issues and limited cost recovery
mentions.detail: Defects identified years after production; recovery from suppliers limited by their financial condition
mentions.quote: Our ability to recover costs associated with recalls or other campaigns caused by parts or components purchased from suppliers may be limited by the suppliers’ financial condition or a number of other reasons or defenses.

mentions.heading: We may incur additional tax expense, become subject to additional tax exposure, or fail to fully realize available tax incentives
mentions.risk_name: Tax law changes and IRA incentive realization
mentions.detail: IRS audits; changes to the Act and IRA; possible controversy over full realization of IRA incentives
mentions.quote: the possibility of tax controversy related to adverse determinations with respect to the application of existing laws (for example, with respect to full realization of the incentives contemplated by the IRA), changes in our business or structure and changes in the valuation of our deferred tax assets and liabilities.

mentions.heading: We rely on GM Financial to provide financial services to our customers and dealers
mentions.risk_name: Captive finance arm funding and credit risk
mentions.detail: GM Financial funding via credit facilities, securitizations, debt; loan performance, used vehicle auction values, residuals, rates affect vehicle sales support
mentions.quote: GM Financial faces a number of business, economic, and financial risks that could impair its access to capital and negatively affect its business and operations, which in turn could impede its ability to provide leasing and financing to customers and commercial lending to our dealers.

mentions.heading: GM Financial must comply with a wide variety of financial services laws
mentions.detail: GM Financial subject to consumer protection laws; penalties, license revocation possible
mentions.quote: The failure to comply with these laws could result in significant statutory civil and criminal penalties, monetary damages, attorneys’ fees and costs, revocation of licenses, and damage to reputation, brand, and valued customer relationships.

mentions.heading: Pension funding requirements could increase significantly
mentions.detail: U.S. and non-U.S. plans; equity and fixed income holdings; some non-U.S. plans unfunded, paid as benefits due
mentions.quote: Certain plans outside the U.S. do not have assets and therefore the obligation is funded as benefits are paid. If local legal authorities increase the minimum funding requirements for our non-U.S. plans, we could be required to contribute more funds, which could negatively affect our liquidity and financial condition.

mentions.heading: The semiconductor industry is highly cyclical.
mentions.detail: Capacity additions cause overcapacity, price and margin erosion, high inventory and under-utilization of manufacturing capacity
mentions.quote:
Investments in new capacity
16

can result in overcapacity, which can lead to a reduction in prices and margins.

mentions.heading: Significantly increased volatility and instability and unfavorable economic conditions may adversely affect our business.
mentions.risk_name: Macroeconomic demand volatility in automotive end markets
mentions.detail: 2020 automotive demand collapse from pandemic shutdowns; 2020-2022 rebound exceeded supply; softening demand 2023-2025 from macro and geopolitics
mentions.quote: In the first half of 2020, demand in the automotive market steeply declined as a result of manufacturing shutdowns by automotive customers due to the coronavirus pandemic, resulting in an unforeseen negative impact to our results of operations.

mentions.heading: The semiconductor industry is highly competitive. If we fail to introduce new technologies and products in a timely manner, this could adversely affect our business.
mentions.risk_name: Technological obsolescence and competitive price erosion
mentions.detail: Rapid tech change, inflation-driven R&D cost increases, larger competitors and consolidation; need to support on-device AI applications
mentions.quote: Meeting evolving industry requirements, including the increasing use of AI and machine learning technologies (including the need to run complex AI-based applications on devices), and introducing new products to the market in a timely manner and at prices that are acceptable to our customers are significant factors in determining our competitiveness and success.

mentions.heading: Risks from introduction and incorporation of AI technologies
mentions.detail: AI may give biased outputs, become obsolete, raise cyber risk; undeveloped AI legal landscape could impose costs
mentions.quote: In addition, AI and machine learning are still in relatively early stages, and the introduction and incorporation of AI technologies may result in unintended consequences or other new or expanded risks and liabilities.

mentions.heading: The demand for our products depends to a significant degree on the demand for our customers’ end products.
mentions.risk_name: End-market demand volatility and order fluctuation
mentions.detail: Revenue mostly from Automotive, Industrial & IoT, Mobile, Communication Infrastructure; customers vary orders, postpone deliveries, cut lead times
mentions.quote: The vast majority of our revenue is derived from sales to manufacturers in the Automotive, Industrial & IoT, Mobile, and Communication Infrastructure end markets. Demand in these markets fluctuates significantly, driven by consumer spending, consumer preferences, the development of new technologies and prevailing economic conditions.

mentions.heading: The semiconductor industry is historically characterized by continued price erosion
mentions.risk_name: Semiconductor price erosion on older products
mentions.detail: Must cut production/procurement costs; may be unable to cease production of legacy products due to contracts or customer relationships
mentions.quote: Moreover, we may not be able to cease production of such products, either due to contractual obligations or for customer relationship reasons, and as a result may be required to bear reduced profitability, or even a loss on such products.

mentions.heading: Dependence on winning selection processes in many market segments
mentions.detail: Long automotive design cycles mean a lost design-in can block customer access for several years
mentions.quote: This risk is particularly pronounced in markets where there are only a few potential customers and in the automotive market, where, due to the longer design cycles involved, failure to win a design-in could prevent access to a customer for several years.

mentions.heading: Global operations expose us to international business risks
mentions.risk_name: Tariffs and export controls disrupting trade
mentions.detail: New or increased US and China tariffs, enhanced export controls and sector sanctions
mentions.quote: negative economic developments in economies around the world and the instability of governments and international trade arrangements, such as the increase of barriers to international trade including the imposition of new or increased tariffs on imports by the United States and China and other countries, enhanced export controls on certain products and sanctions on certain industry sectors and parties;

mentions.heading: Social and political instability including Middle East and Ukraine
mentions.risk_name: Armed conflict disrupting supply and demand
mentions.detail: Middle East hostilities and Ukraine conflict affect customers, supply chain, energy prices
mentions.quote: social and political instability in a number of countries around the world, including continued hostilities in the Middle East and the armed conflict in Ukraine.

mentions.heading: Epidemics and pandemics
mentions.risk_name: Pandemic disruption to workforce and suppliers
mentions.detail: Generic statement; cites coronavirus
mentions.quote: epidemics and pandemics, such as the coronavirus outbreak, which may adversely affect our workforce, as well as our suppliers and customers;

mentions.heading: Geopolitical tension and disputes
mentions.detail: China-Taiwan tensions, restricted entity lists could decouple global trade and technology supply chains
mentions.quote: Sustained geopolitical tensions, such as the current geopolitical tensions involving China and Taiwan, could lead to long-term changes in global trade and technology supply chains and decoupling of global trade networks;

mentions.heading: Foreign currency volatility and transfer restrictions
mentions.risk_name: Currency volatility and cash transfer restrictions
mentions.detail: U.S. dollar exposure; transfer restrictions in mainland China
mentions.quote: volatility in foreign currency exchange rates, in particular with respect to the U.S. dollar, and transfer restrictions, in particular in mainland China; and

mentions.heading: Recently announced and future tariffs and other trade restrictions could materially and adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: 2025 US tariffs, US-China trade tension; April 2025 Section 232 investigation into imported semiconductors and equipment; copper, critical minerals probes
mentions.quote: For example, in April 2025, the Department of Commerce launched an investigation into the national security impacts of imported semiconductors and semiconductor manufacturing equipment. While the results of this investigation remain unknown, it is expected to result in additional tariffs and trade restrictions that may adversely impact our business.

drivers.name: Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962

mentions.heading: Goodwill and intangible assets are significant; may never realize full value
mentions.detail: Acquisition-related goodwill and intangibles are a significant portion of total assets; IP validity challenges could trigger impairment
mentions.quote: Any future determination of impairment of goodwill or other identifiable intangible assets could have a material adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations and stockholders’ equity.

mentions.heading: In difficult market conditions, our high fixed costs combined with low revenue may negatively affect our results of operations
mentions.risk_name: Fab underutilization with high fixed costs
mentions.detail: Own fabrication plants; utilization declined in first half of 2020 downturn, lowering gross profit
mentions.quote: During such periods, our fabrication plants could operate at lower loading level, while the fixed costs associated with the full capacity continue to be incurred, resulting in lower gross profit.

mentions.heading: We may from time to time restructure parts of our organization
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: The costs of implementing any restructurings, changes or cost savings steps may differ from our estimates and any negative impacts on our revenues or otherwise of such restructurings, changes or steps, such as situations in which customer satisfaction is negatively impacted, may be larger than originally estimated.

mentions.heading: Failure to renegotiate collective bargaining agreements or consult works councils could harm business
mentions.risk_name: Labor union and works council disruption
mentions.detail: Collective bargaining agreements, social plans; works council consultation required for restructurings, acquisitions and divestitures
mentions.quote: We are also required to consult with our employee representatives, such as works councils, on items such as restructurings, acquisitions and divestitures.

mentions.heading: Our working capital needs are difficult to predict.
mentions.risk_name: Working capital volatility from long product cycles
mentions.detail: Long development-to-delivery period drives high inventory and WIP; stockpiling across many specifications
mentions.quote: The comparatively long period between the time at which we commence development of a product and the time at which it may be delivered to a customer leads to high inventory and work-in-progress levels.

mentions.heading: Costs relating to product defects, product liability and warranty claims
mentions.detail: Replacement cost of defective semiconductors often exceeds device value; customer recalls may be charged back; personal injury exposure
mentions.quote: Moreover, since the cost of replacing defective semiconductor devices is often much higher than the value of the devices themselves, we may at times face damage claims from customers in excess of the amounts they pay us for our products, including consequential damages.

mentions.heading: We face risks related to security vulnerabilities in our products.
mentions.detail: Processors used in cloud, IoT, critical infrastructure and automotive applications, increasing cybersecurity and safety exposure
mentions.quote: This includes applications that gather and process large amounts of data, such as the cloud or Internet of Things, and critical infrastructure and automotive applications.

mentions.heading: Our business has suffered, and could in the future suffer, from manufacturing problems.
mentions.risk_name: Fab manufacturing disruptions and yield problems
mentions.detail: Austin, Texas fabs disrupted by February 2021 winter storm; utility rationing of electricity, gas, water cited
mentions.quote: Further, we may suffer disruptions in our manufacturing operations, either due to production difficulties such as those described above or as a result of external factors beyond our control, such as the disruption to our Austin, Texas manufacturing facilities caused by the February 2021 winter storm.

mentions.heading: We rely on the timely supply of equipment and materials and could suffer if suppliers fail to meet their delivery obligations or raise prices.
mentions.risk_name: Limited-source equipment and materials supply shortage
mentions.detail: Shortages of silicon wafers and specialized chemicals; few suppliers; tariffs and trade restrictions may raise costs
mentions.quote: Supply disruptions may also occur due to shortages in critical materials, such as silicon wafers or specialized chemicals. In addition, the imposition of tariffs or other trade restrictions may significantly increase the costs, and otherwise adversely impact the availability of certain raw materials and supplies needed for our manufacturing operations.

mentions.heading: Failure of our third party suppliers to perform could adversely affect our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Could not obtain sufficient silicon wafers from foundry partners during 2022 shortage; outsourcing costs rise; long-term supply agreements with key partners
mentions.quote: For example, as part of the industry-wide shortage of semiconductors during 2022 we could not obtain sufficient silicon wafers from our foundry partners to meet the demand for our products, causing us not to fully supply the demand for our products, and negatively affecting our results of operations.

mentions.heading: Disruptions in our relationships with any one of our key customers could adversely affect our business.
mentions.detail: Substantial revenue from top customers including distributors; no names or percentages given
mentions.quote: A substantial portion of our revenue is derived from our top customers, including our distributors. We cannot guarantee that we will be able to generate similar levels of revenue from our largest customers in the future.

mentions.heading: We receive subsidies and grants in certain countries, and a reduction in governmental funding or demands for repayment could increase our costs.
mentions.detail: Receives government subsidies and grants in some countries; agencies could recover subsidies if grant conditions unmet
mentions.quote: In such event that we don't meet the subsidies grant conditions, such government agencies could seek to recover such subsidies from us, and they could cancel or reduce other subsidies we receive from them.

mentions.heading: Certain natural disasters may negatively impact our business; climate change may increase natural disasters.
mentions.risk_name: Natural disaster and climate operational disruption
mentions.detail: Cites flooding, heavy precipitation, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, nuclear disasters; climate change increasing frequency
mentions.quote: Environmental and other disasters, such as flooding, heavy precipitation large earthquakes, volcanic eruptions or nuclear or other disasters, or a combination thereof may negatively impact our business.

mentions.heading: Natural disasters and climate change could disrupt manufacturing facilities
mentions.detail: Factories in earthquake/flood/storm zones in Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia, Thailand; February 2021 winter storm disrupted Austin, Texas fabs
mentions.quote: The impact of any such natural disasters depends on the specific geographic circumstances but could be significant, as some of our factories are located in areas with known earthquake fault zones, flood or storm risks, including but not limited to Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia or Thailand.

mentions.heading: Water scarcity at semi-arid manufacturing sites
mentions.detail: Water-intensive semiconductor manufacturing; many own and supplier sites in semi-arid regions vulnerable to drought
mentions.quote: In addition, semiconductor manufacturing is a water-intensive process. Many of our manufacturing sites and those of our suppliers are located in semi–arid regions that may become increasingly vulnerable to prolonged droughts associated with evolving changes to the climate, which may lead to water scarcity.

mentions.heading: Acquisitions and strategic transactions could adversely affect results
mentions.detail: Routine acquisitions, JVs, minority stakes and loans; government agencies have denied or delayed approvals in the past
mentions.quote: Certain agencies in the past have, and may in the future, deny the transaction or fail to approve in a timely manner, resulting in delays in closing and us not realizing the anticipated benefits of the proposed transactions.

mentions.heading: Reliance on joint ventures we do not control for manufacturing
mentions.detail: Hybrid manufacturing via SSMC with TSMC, VSMC with Vanguard, ESMC with TSMC, Bosch, Infineon
mentions.quote: For example, we currently participate in a joint venture with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (“TSMC”) called Systems on Silicon Manufacturing Company Pte. Ltd. (“SSMC”) and have recently formed a joint venture with Vanguard International Semiconductor Corporation called VisionPower Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Pte. Ltd. (“VSMC”), and a joint venture with TSMC, Robert Bosch Gmbh and Infineon Technologies AG called European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (“ESMC”) to create capability for our future manufacturing requirements.

mentions.heading: Joint ventures and alliances may not achieve anticipated benefits
mentions.risk_name: Joint venture funding and execution shortfall
mentions.detail: Alliances may carry funding or take-or-pay obligations; new JVs may miss production timing or quality targets
mentions.quote: Under the terms of current or future alliances, we may have certain obligations, including funding obligations or take or pay obligations.

mentions.heading: As our business is global, we need to comply with laws and regulations in countries across the world.
mentions.detail: U.S. EAR and EU sanctions; ceased shipments to Huawei in 2020; new U.S. administration policy changes
mentions.quote: For example, in 2020, due to regulations imposed by the U.S. government, we ceased shipments of our products to Huawei pending approval of export licenses.

mentions.heading: Global privacy legislation creating complex compliance environment
mentions.detail: EU GDPR and expanding global privacy rules; compliance costs could be significant
mentions.quote: Furthermore, global privacy legislation, enforcement, and policy activity, such as the EU General Data Privacy Regulation, are rapidly expanding and creating a complex regulatory compliance environment. Costs to comply with and implement these privacy-related and data protection measures could be significant.

mentions.heading: Restrictions on cross-border semiconductor investments
mentions.detail: Dutch foreign investment control regime and U.S. outbound investment rules may limit acquisitions and alliances
mentions.quote: In addition, governments are increasingly imposing restrictions on cross-border investments in semiconductor businesses and technology, such as the Dutch foreign investment control regime and U.S. outbound investment rules, that may limit our ability to execute strategic acquisitions, investments and alliances, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business.

mentions.heading: Legal proceedings covering a range of matters are pending in various jurisdictions.
mentions.detail: Past personal injury claims over chemical exposure in clean rooms operated by NXP or former parents Philips and Motorola
mentions.quote: Furthermore, because we continue to utilize these clean rooms, we may become subject to future claims alleging personal injury that may lead to additional liability.

mentions.heading: Environmental, health and safety laws and permits compliance
mentions.detail: Strict, joint and several liability at current and historical manufacturing facilities for hazardous substance contamination
mentions.quote: As with other companies engaged in similar activities or that own or operate real property, we face inherent risks of environmental liability at our current and historical manufacturing facilities.

mentions.heading: Climate change initiatives may increase production costs
mentions.risk_name: Climate regulation raising energy and production costs
mentions.detail: Carbon taxes, carbon offsets, higher energy prices and lower-carbon equipment or materials could raise production costs
mentions.quote: Public and private initiatives to address climate change may result in an increase in the cost of production due to increase in the prices of energy, introduction of energy or carbon tax or the purchase of carbon offsets.

mentions.heading: Interruptions in our information technology systems could adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Any significant interruption in our business applications, systems or networks, including but not limited to new system implementations, computer viruses, cyberattacks, security breaches, facility issues or energy blackouts could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

mentions.heading: Computer systems subject to attempted security breaches and cybersecurity incidents
mentions.detail: Has experienced cyber-attacks; risk of misappropriating proprietary technology; AI-enabled attacks cited
mentions.quote: For example, as AI continues to evolve, cyber attackers could also use AI to develop malicious code and increasingly sophisticated phishing attempts.

mentions.heading: Cybersecurity and privacy breach risks
mentions.detail: Generic threats including state-sponsored intrusions; rising security spend
mentions.quote: Computer hackers and others routinely attempt to breach the security of technology products, services, and systems, and those of customers, suppliers, and some of those attempts may be successful.

mentions.heading: Employee misappropriation of proprietary technology
mentions.detail: Identified instances of former employees misappropriating technology, some possibly violating export controls, reported to authorities
mentions.quote: We have identified instances of employee misappropriation or theft of certain proprietary technology by individuals who are no longer employed by NXP. In some cases, such misappropriation may result in the violation of applicable export control regulations, which we report to relevant authorities as appropriate.

mentions.heading: We may not be able to protect our proprietary intellectual property against improper use by competitors or others.
mentions.risk_name: Intellectual property misappropriation and weak enforcement
mentions.detail: Relies on patents, trade secrets for designs and fabrication processes; enforcement difficult in some countries of operation
mentions.quote: In particular, intellectual property rights are difficult to enforce in countries where the application and enforcement of the laws governing such rights may not have reached the same level as compared to other jurisdictions where we operate.

mentions.heading: Unsettled IP rights surrounding AI technologies built into products
mentions.risk_name: Uncertain IP ownership of AI technologies
mentions.detail: AI built into products and used in development; IP ownership unaddressed by U.S. or foreign courts and laws
mentions.quote: Finally, the intellectual property ownership and license rights, including copyrights and patents, surrounding AI technologies, which we are and may in the future continue to build into our products, have not been fully addressed by U.S. or foreign courts, laws or regulations, and the use of AI in the development of our products and services could result in our loss of, or failure to obtain, intellectual property rights, as well as subject us to risks related to intellectual property infringement or misappropriation.

mentions.heading: We may become party to intellectual property claims or litigation that could cause us to incur substantial costs
mentions.risk_name: Patent infringement litigation and injunction exposure
mentions.detail: Has received infringement communications; treble damages possible in United States; injunctions could halt product sales
mentions.quote: In the event that we cannot obtain or take the view that we don’t need a license, these parties may file lawsuits against us seeking damages (and potentially treble damages in the United States) or an injunction against the sale of our products that incorporate allegedly infringed intellectual property or against the operation of our business as presently conducted.

mentions.heading: AI use may expose company to IP claims
mentions.detail: Use of AI for productivity and in products may trigger copyright or IP misappropriation claims amid legal uncertainty
mentions.quote: Additionally, and in part due to ongoing uncertainties in the legal framework around AI, our use of AI technologies for productivity and in our products and services may expose us to copyright infringement or other intellectual property misappropriation claims.

mentions.heading: Loss of our key management and other personnel could affect our business
mentions.detail: Depends on senior engineers; competitive market for skilled engineers
mentions.quote: The market for qualified employees, including skilled engineers and other individuals with the required technical expertise to succeed in our business, is highly competitive and the loss of qualified employees or an inability to attract, retain and motivate the additional highly skilled employees required for the operation and expansion of our business could hinder our ability to successfully conduct research activities or develop marketable products.

mentions.heading: CEO transition may not be successful
mentions.detail: Kurt Sievers retired October 28, 2025; Rafael Sotomayor succeeded as President and CEO
mentions.quote: Effective October 28, 2025, Kurt Sievers voluntarily retired as our CEO and executive director and Rafael Sotomayor succeeded Mr. Sievers as President and CEO and temporary executive director of the Company.

mentions.heading: United States civil liabilities may not be enforceable against us
mentions.risk_name: Foreign incorporation limits US judgment enforcement
mentions.detail: Incorporated in the Netherlands; substantial assets and some directors and officers outside the United States
mentions.quote: We are incorporated under the laws of the Netherlands and substantial portions of our assets are located outside of the United States. In addition, certain members of our board and officers reside outside the United States.

mentions.heading: Difficulty enforcing U.S. judgments against the Company and its directors in the Netherlands
mentions.detail: No US-Netherlands treaty on mutual judgment enforcement; claims must be relitigated before Dutch courts
mentions.quote: In order to obtain a judgment which is enforceable in the Netherlands, the claim must be relitigated before a competent court of the Netherlands; the relevant Netherlands court has discretion to attach such weight to a judgment of the courts of the United States as it deems appropriate;

mentions.heading: We are a Dutch public company with limited liability. The rights of our stockholders may be different from the rights of stockholders governed by the laws of U.S. jurisdictions.
mentions.detail: Dutch naamloze vennootschap; board must by Dutch law weigh company, employee and stakeholder interests, not only stockholders
mentions.quote: In the performance of its duties, our board of directors is required by Dutch law to consider the interests of our company, its stockholders, its employees and other stakeholders, in all cases with due observation of the principles of reasonableness and fairness.

mentions.heading: Our debt obligations expose us to risks that could adversely affect our financial condition
mentions.risk_name: Substantial indebtedness and debt service burden
mentions.detail: $12,290 million principal debt outstanding at December 31, 2025; cash flow diverted to principal and interest
mentions.quote: As of December 31, 2025, we had outstanding indebtedness with an aggregate principal amount of $12,290 million. Our substantial indebtedness could have a material adverse effect on our business by:

mentions.heading: Exposure to increased interest rates on revolving credit facility borrowings
mentions.detail: $2,500 million RCF restated to $3,000 million on February 6, 2026; loans may bear variable interest
mentions.quote: •exposing us to the risk of increased interest rates in the event we have borrowings under our $2,500 million revolving credit facility agreement (the “RCF Agreement”), which was restated to $3,000 million as per February 6, 2026, because loans under the RCF Agreement may bear interest at a variable rate;

mentions.heading: Consequences of substantial leverage (bullet list continuation)
mentions.detail: Leverage may trigger indenture defaults, restrict acquisitions, limit financing and cause competitive disadvantage
mentions.quote: limiting our ability to obtain additional financial for working capital, capital expenditures, restructurings, product development, research and development, debt service requirements, investments, acquisitions and general corporate or other purposes; and

mentions.heading: Despite our level of indebtedness, we may still incur significantly more debt
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Despite our level of indebtedness, we may still incur significantly more debt, which could further exacerbate the risks described above and affect our ability to service and repay our debt.

mentions.heading: If we do not comply with the covenants in our debt agreements or fail to generate sufficient cash to service and repay our debt, it could adversely affect our operating results and our financial condition.
mentions.detail: Covenants under RCF Agreement, EIB loan facilities and unsecured note indentures; acceleration could cause cross defaults
mentions.quote: The RCF Agreement, European Investment Bank (EIB) loan facilities and the indentures governing our unsecured notes or any other debt arrangements that we may have require us to comply with various covenants.

mentions.heading: If we do not comply with the covenants in our debt agreements or fail to generate sufficient cash to service and repay our debt
mentions.risk_name: Refinancing risk and insufficient debt service cash
mentions.detail: Refinancing dependent on capital markets; may be at higher rates with more onerous covenants
mentions.quote: Our ability to restructure or refinance our debt will depend on the condition of the capital markets and our financial condition at such time. Any refinancing of our debt could be at higher interest rates and may require us to comply with more onerous covenants, which could further restrict our business operations.

mentions.heading: The rating of our debt by major rating agencies may further improve or deteriorate, which could affect our additional borrowing capacity and financing costs.
mentions.risk_name: Credit rating downgrade raising borrowing costs
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Actual or anticipated changes or downgrades in our credit ratings, including any announcement that our ratings are under further review for a downgrade, could affect our market value and/or increase our corporate borrowing costs.

mentions.heading: The price of our common stock may fluctuate significantly
mentions.risk_name: Stock price volatility and securities litigation
mentions.detail: Closing price ranged from $245.86 (Feb 20, 2025) to $153.50 (Apr 8, 2025)
mentions.quote: The market closing price for our common stock varied between a high of $245.86 on February 20, 2025, and a low of $153.50 on April 8, 2025, in the twelve-month period ending on December 31, 2025.

mentions.heading: Fluctuations in the amount and frequency of stock repurchases
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: The amount, timing, and execution of our stock repurchases may fluctuate based on our priorities for the use of cash for other purposes—such as investing in our business, including operational spending, capital spending, and acquisitions, and returning cash to our stockholders as dividend payments—and because of changes in cash flows, tax laws, and the market price of our common stock.

mentions.heading: No assurance of continued cash dividends
mentions.detail: Quarterly cash dividend policy; restricted by law, contracts and corporate structure
mentions.quote: The declaration and payment of any dividend is subject to the approval of our board, and our dividend may be discontinued or reduced at any time.

mentions.heading: Financial markets and demographics may raise defined benefit pension costs
mentions.detail: Net accrued benefit liability of $342 million at December 31, 2025 across plans in multiple countries
mentions.quote: As of December 31, 2025, we had recognized a net accrued benefit liability of $342 million, representing the unfunded benefit obligations of our defined pension plans.

mentions.heading: Future changes to Dutch, U.S. and other foreign tax laws could adversely affect us.
mentions.detail: EU Pillar 2 directive effective 2024, enacted in Dutch legislation; OECD/G7 June 2025 side-by-side safe harbor may amend rules
mentions.quote: As part of the OECD framework to implement a minimum tax rate, the EU has adopted a directive on ensuring a global minimum level of taxation for multinational companies, also known as Pillar 2, which became effective in 2024.

mentions.heading: We are exposed to a number of different tax uncertainties, which could have an impact on our results.
mentions.risk_name: Transfer pricing disputes and tax asset challenges
mentions.detail: Transfer-pricing directives on goods, services, financing per OECD guidelines; acquisition-related tax assets and loss carryforwards may be challenged
mentions.quote: Transfer pricing uncertainties can also result from disputes with local tax authorities about transfer pricing of internal deliveries of goods and services or related to financing, acquisitions and divestments, the use of tax credits and permanent establishments, and tax losses carried forward.

mentions.heading: Our global operations subject us to risks associated with domestic or international political, social, economic or other conditions.
mentions.detail: About 50% of 2025 revenue shipped into China, 20% from China-headquartered customers; tariffs, export restrictions on semiconductors
mentions.quote: Revenue from end customers headquartered in China represented about 20% of our revenue in 2025, while revenue from products shipped into China represented about 50% of our revenue in 2025.

mentions.heading: Exposure to conditions and currency fluctuations across operating countries
mentions.detail: Facilities in 30+ countries; about 60% of revenue from customers headquartered outside US
mentions.quote: In addition, our global operations expose us to periods when the U.S. dollar significantly fluctuates in relation to the non-U.S. currencies in which we transact business. The remeasurement of non-U.S. dollar transactions can have an adverse effect on our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: We face substantial competition that requires us to respond rapidly to product development and pricing pressures.
mentions.detail: China promoting domestic semiconductor industry via policy and investment; emerging Asian competitors pressure pricing and margins
mentions.quote: For example, we may face increased competition as a result of China actively promoting and reshaping its domestic semiconductor industry through policy changes and investment, which could prevent us from competing effectively.

mentions.heading: Changes in expected demand for our products could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Semiconductor cyclicality; large customer curtailments from sourcing changes, inventory adjustments, tariffs or export controls
mentions.quote: The cyclical nature of the semiconductor market occasionally leads to significant and rapid increases and decreases in product demand.

mentions.heading: Changes in expected demand for our products could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.
mentions.risk_name: Large customer purchase curtailment from trade measures
mentions.detail: Loss of large customers due to sourcing policy changes, tariffs, export controls or other trade measures
mentions.quote: Additionally, the loss or significant curtailment of purchases by one or more of our large customers, including curtailments due to a change in the design or manufacturing sourcing policies or practices of these customers, the timing of customer or distributor inventory adjustments, changes in demand for customer products, tariffs, export controls or other trade measures, may adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Ability to match inventory and production with product mix
mentions.detail: Manufactures ahead for high customer service; inaccurate forecasts cause excess or obsolete inventory
mentions.quote: Our manufacturing forecasts are based on multiple assumptions, and if inaccurate, could cause us to hold inadequate, excess or obsolete inventory that would reduce our profit margins and adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Our operating results and our reputation could be adversely affected by cybersecurity events, breaches, disruptions or other incidents relating to our information technology systems.
mentions.detail: Generic statement; mentions nation-state espionage and AI tools as threat vectors
mentions.quote: Cybersecurity or other threats to our information technology systems or the systems of our customers, suppliers and other third parties are frequent, increasingly sophisticated and constantly evolving, thereby making them more difficult to detect, mitigate and defend against.

mentions.heading: Our ability to successfully implement strategic, business and organizational changes could affect our business plans and results of operations.
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: We may not achieve or sustain the expected growth, cost savings or other benefits of strategic, business and organizational changes, and charges associated with these actions could differ materially in amount and timing from our expectations.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations could be affected by natural events in the locations in which we operate.
mentions.risk_name: Natural disaster disruption of manufacturing sites
mentions.detail: Manufacturing, data and design facilities exposed to severe weather, geological events, epidemics; climate change may worsen frequency
mentions.quote: Climate change might exacerbate these occurrences or cause natural disasters to occur with greater frequency and with more intense effects.

mentions.heading: Rapid technological change in markets we serve requires us to develop new technologies and products.
mentions.risk_name: Technological change shortening product life cycles
mentions.detail: Significant R&D investment made before commercial viability; returns may lag several years; ASP declines
mentions.quote: Rapid technological change in markets we serve could contribute to shortened product life cycles and a decline in average selling prices of our products.

mentions.heading: We face supply chain and manufacturing risks.
mentions.detail: Key materials sourced from limited geographies; export controls on minerals, materials and equipment; suppliers extending lead times
mentions.quote: Further, certain key materials used in semiconductor manufacturing are primarily sourced from limited geographies. Governments have adopted or proposed measures, including export controls on certain minerals, materials and equipment, that could adversely affect equipment and material availability, cost or movement.

mentions.heading: We face supply chain and manufacturing risks.
mentions.risk_name: Dependence on subcontracted wafer fabrication suppliers
mentions.detail: Subcontracts wafer fab, assembly/test and advanced logic process development; no long-term contracts with all; few alternates
mentions.quote: We do not have long-term contracts with all of these suppliers, and the number of alternate suppliers is limited.

mentions.heading: Ability to retain, train and recruit qualified employees in a competitive environment
mentions.detail: Engineering and technical talent competition; international recruiting constrained by immigration laws and policies
mentions.quote: Our ability to recruit internationally or deploy employees to various locations may be limited by immigration laws and policies, including changes to, or the administration or interpretation of, those laws and policies.

mentions.heading: Warranty claims, product liability claims, product recalls or legal proceedings
mentions.risk_name: Product liability and customer recall costs
mentions.detail: Customer recalls of products containing TI parts, e.g. automotive and handheld electronics; inventory write-offs; insurance may be inadequate
mentions.quote: In addition, it is possible for a customer to recall a product containing a TI part, for example with respect to products used in automotive applications or handheld electronics, which may cause us to incur costs and expenses relating to the recall.

mentions.heading: Distributors' promotion of competing product lines or distributors' financial performance
mentions.risk_name: Distributor competing lines and credit exposure
mentions.detail: Less than 20% of 2025 revenue through distributors carrying competing lines; nonpayment and administrative measure risk
mentions.quote: In 2025, less than 20% of our revenue was generated from sales of our products through distributors. Our distributors carry competing product lines, and our sales could be affected if semiconductor distributors promote competing products over our products.

mentions.heading: Our margins vary
mentions.detail: Owns much of manufacturing capacity; capacity expansions raised capex and depreciation; fixed costs don't fall with demand; tariffs, freight
mentions.quote: Because we own much of our manufacturing capacity, a significant portion of our operating costs is fixed. With our capacity expansions, capital expenditures and depreciation have increased.

mentions.heading: Our operations could be affected by the complex laws, rules and regulations to which our business is subject.
mentions.detail: Generic list of regulated areas; government inquiries could lead to enforcement or fines
mentions.quote: Compliance with these laws, rules and regulations may be onerous and expensive and could restrict our ability to manufacture or ship our products and operate our business.

mentions.heading: Environmental, safety and health rules affecting manufacturing jurisdictions
mentions.detail: Possible abatement equipment requirements, material/process bans, energy and emissions fees; substitutes may be unavailable or costly
mentions.quote: A substitute for a prohibited material or process might not be available, or might not be available at reasonable cost.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations could be affected by changes in tax-related matters.
mentions.detail: Facilities in 30+ countries; deferred tax assets realizability; OECD BEPS rules uncertain for U.S. multinationals
mentions.quote: In addition, many countries have enacted or begun the process of enacting laws that align with the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development’s Base Erosion and Profit Shifting recommendations; application of these laws to U.S.-based multinational corporations remains uncertain.

drivers.name: Base Erosion and Profit Shifting recommendations

mentions.heading: Government incentives could be reduced, modified or clawed back
mentions.detail: Received tax and other government incentives for investments; scrutiny on how earned and spent
mentions.quote: Such incentives could be subject to reduction, modification, clawback or termination, and such changes to these incentives could adversely affect our results of operations, financial condition and reputation.

mentions.heading: Our performance depends in part on our ability to enforce our intellectual property rights and to maintain freedom of operation.
mentions.detail: Claims from nonpracticing entities; customer indemnification obligations; counterfeiting, cloning; weaker foreign IP laws
mentions.quote: We, directly and indirectly, face infringement claims from third parties, including nonpracticing entities that have acquired patents to pursue enforcement actions against other companies.

mentions.heading: Our debt could affect our operations and financial condition.
mentions.risk_name: Debt service burden on cash flow
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: In addition, our obligation to make principal and interest payments could divert funds that otherwise might be invested in our operations or returned to shareholders, or could cause us to raise funds by, for example, issuing new debt or equity or selling assets.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations and liquidity could be affected by changes in the financial markets.
mentions.detail: Relies on bank credit lines backing commercial paper and revolving credit facilities
mentions.quote: If we are unable to access these accounts and credit lines (for example, due to instability in the financial markets), our results of operations and financial condition could be adversely affected and our ability to access the capital markets or redeem our investments could be restricted.

mentions.heading: Material impairments of our goodwill could adversely affect our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: We have a significant amount of goodwill on our consolidated balance sheet. Charges associated with impairments of goodwill could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
